passage:
On a small island, students go to school by boat. When the sea is calm, the trip takes fifteen minutes. When the weather is bad, classes may start late.
A new student named Victor complained at first. He came from the city, where school was only five minutes away.
One morning, dolphins appeared near the boat. Everyone watched quietly. Another day, the sunrise turned the water orange. Victor took a picture and sent it to his old friends.
Slowly, he stopped seeing the boat ride only as a problem. It was still inconvenient sometimes, but it also gave him something city students did not have.
The way to school became part of the lesson.
